source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substring including written/read and other annotations.
source.public_versification_note: Exact XML records mapped to public labels; Zechariah 1:18–2:13 and Malachi 4 have different Hebrew chapter boundaries.

delta_method: F0 retained; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential choices flagged by the selective apparatus. Classification remains provisional. Overlap is triage only, with no change quota.

comparative_references.scope: Programmatic alignment after recovery of unfinished original-language drafts; selected bilingual rereads recorded separately. TSW is not the base text.

verses.rationale: Retains all four ancestral generations and the exact royal setting.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sweeping totality and ground image.
verses.before: “I will sweep away, sweep away everything from the face of the earth,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: “I will sweep everything away from the face of the ground,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will sweep away, sweep away everything from the face of the earth,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains all creature categories and the difficult stumbling-blocks phrase without deleting it.
verses.before: “I will sweep away human beings and animals; I will sweep away the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling blocks along with the wicked. I will cut off humanity from the face of the earth,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: “I will sweep away humans and animals; I will sweep away the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea, the stumbling blocks along with the wicked. I will cut humanity off from the face of the ground,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will sweep away human beings and animals; I will sweep away the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling blocks along with the wicked. I will cut off humanity from the face of the earth,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two priest terms distinguishable and the continuing list open.
verses.before: “I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the idolatrous priests along with the priests;
verses.after: “I will stretch out my hand against Judah and everyone who lives in Jerusalem. From this place I will cut off what remains of Baal, the name of the idol-priests along with the priests,
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the idolatrous priests along with the priests;

verses.rationale: Follows the pointed their-king reading and notes the Milcom alternative.
verses.before: people who bow down on the rooftops to the host of the heavens; people who bow down, who swear by the LORD and swear by Milcom;
verses.after: those who bow on the rooftops to heaven’s army, those who bow and swear allegiance to the LORD while also swearing by their king,
verses.tsw_comparator: those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of the heavens; those who bow down, who swear by the LORD and swear by Milcom;

verses.rationale: Preserves both repeated divine names and the paired failures to seek.
verses.before: people who turn back from following the LORD, who have not sought the LORD or inquired of him.”
verses.after: those who turn away from following the LORD, who neither seek the LORD nor inquire of him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: those who turn back from following the LORD, who have not sought the LORD or inquired of him.”

verses.rationale: Retains the unsettling sacrifice/guest image without assigning each participant.
verses.before: Be silent before the Lord GOD! For the day of the LORD is near. For the LORD has prepared a sacrifice; he has consecrated his invited guests.
verses.after: Be silent before the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is near! The LORD has prepared a sacrifice and consecrated his invited guests.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be silent before the Lord GOD! For the day of the LORD is near. For the LORD has prepared a sacrifice; he has consecrated his invited guests.

verses.rationale: Keeps royal sons and clothing as stated rather than interpreting their precise offense.
verses.before: “And on the day of the LORD’s sacrifice, I will punish the officials and the king’s sons, and everyone who wear foreign clothing.
verses.after: “On the day of the LORD’s sacrifice I will punish the officials, the king’s sons, and everyone dressed in foreign clothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And on the day of the LORD’s sacrifice, I will punish the officials and the king’s sons, and all who wear foreign clothing.

verses.rationale: Retains the obscure threshold practice, with context left to a note.
verses.before: On that day I will punish everyone who leap over the threshold, who fill their masters’ houses with violence and deceit.
verses.after: On that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold, who fills their master’s house with violence and deceit.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day I will punish all who leap over the threshold, who fill their masters’ houses with violence and deceit.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jerusalem locations and the sequence of sounds.
verses.before: “And on that day,” declares the LORD, “there will be a sound of outcry from the Fish Gate, a wailing from the Second Quarter, and a great crash from the hills.
verses.after: On that day,” declares the LORD, “a cry will rise from the Fish Gate, a wail from the Second Quarter, and a great crash from the hills.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And on that day,” declares the LORD, “there will be a sound of outcry from the Fish Gate, a wailing from the Second Quarter, and a great crash from the hills.

verses.rationale: Chooses merchant for Canaan in the trade context and preserves the district’s literal name.
verses.before: Wail, inhabitants of the Mortar, for all the people of Canaan are silenced; everyone who weigh out silver are cut off.
verses.after: Wail, you who live in the Mortar! All the merchant people are silenced; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wail, inhabitants of the Mortar, for all the people of Canaan are silenced; all who weigh out silver are cut off.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wine-dregs image and the complacent claim in direct speech.
verses.before: “At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish those who have congealed on their dregs, who say in their hearts, ‘The LORD will not do good, nor will he do evil.’
verses.after: At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish the men settled on their dregs, who say in their hearts, ‘The LORD will do neither good nor harm.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish those who have congealed on their dregs, who say in their hearts, ‘The LORD will not do good, nor will he do evil.’

verses.rationale: Retains paired frustrated actions and concrete losses.
verses.before: Their wealth will become plunder and their houses a desolation. They will build houses but not inhabit them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.”
verses.after: Their wealth will become plunder, their houses a desolation. They will build houses but not live in them, plant vineyards but not drink their wine.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Their wealth will become plunder and their houses a desolation. They will build houses but not inhabit them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.”

verses.rationale: Keeps near repeated and the sudden auditory summons.
verses.before: Near is the great day of the LORD, near and coming very quickly. The sound of the day of the LORD— bitter! There the warrior cries out.
verses.after: The great day of the LORD is near— near and coming very quickly! Listen to the day of the LORD: there the warrior cries out bitterly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Near is the great day of the LORD, near and coming very quickly. The sound of the day of the LORD— bitter! There the warrior cries out.

verses.rationale: Retains the anaphoric day-of structure and paired terms.
verses.before: That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of devastation and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness,
verses.after: That day is a day of fury, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,
verses.tsw_comparator: That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of devastation and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness,

verses.rationale: Completes the preceding day list and identifies the defensive corners naturally.
verses.before: a day of trumpet blast and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high towers.
verses.after: a day of horn blast and battle cry against fortified cities and their high corner towers.
verses.tsw_comparator: a day of trumpet blast and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high towers.

verses.rationale: Preserves the violent bodily images and the stated causal connection.
verses.before: “I will bring distress upon people, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.
verses.after: “I will bring distress upon humanity, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, their flesh like dung.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will bring distress upon people, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal scope, jealousy, and the suddenness rather than reducing the warning to wealth alone.
verses.before: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the day of the LORD’s wrath. By the fire of his jealousy the entire earth will be consumed; for he will make a complete end— indeed, a terrifying end— of all the inhabitants of the earth.”
verses.after: Neither their silver nor their gold can rescue them on the day of the LORD’s fury. The whole earth will be consumed by the fire of his jealousy, for he will make a sudden, complete end of everyone who lives on the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the day of the LORD’s wrath. By the fire of his jealousy the whole earth will be consumed; for he will make a complete end— indeed, a terrifying end— of all the inhabitants of the earth.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated gathering call and chooses unwanted for the difficult participle, with alternative noted.
verses.before: Gather yourselves, yes, gather, nation without shame,
verses.after: Gather yourselves; gather together, unwanted nation,
verses.tsw_comparator: Gather yourselves, yes, gather, nation without shame,

verses.rationale: Keeps the birthing decree and chaff images alongside the repeated before clauses.
verses.before: before the decree gives birth— the day passes like chaff— before the burning anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the day of the LORD’s anger comes upon you.
verses.after: before the decree gives birth, before the day passes like chaff, before the LORD’s burning anger comes upon you, before the day of the LORD’s anger comes upon you.
verses.tsw_comparator: before the decree gives birth— the day passes like chaff— before the burning anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the day of the LORD’s anger comes upon you.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three seek commands and the consequential perhaps.
verses.before: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the earth, who carry out his justice; seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD’s anger.
verses.after: Seek the LORD, all you humble people of the earth who carry out his judgment. Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD’s anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the earth, who carry out his justice; seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD’s anger.

verses.rationale: Retains each city, noon, and the uprooting verb that echoes its name.
verses.before: For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon a desolation; at noon they will drive out Ashdod, and Ekron will be uprooted.
verses.after: For Gaza will be abandoned, Ashkelon left desolate. Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron uprooted.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon a desolation; at noon they will drive out Ashdod, and Ekron will be uprooted.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the coast’s named people from the quoted threat.
verses.before: Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, the nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you: Canaan, land of the Philistines, I will destroy you until no inhabitant remains.
verses.after: Woe to those who live along the coast, the nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: “I will destroy you until no inhabitant remains.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, the nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you: Canaan, land of the Philistines, I will destroy you until no inhabitant remains.

verses.rationale: Chooses shelters for the uncertain middle noun without inventing a geographic detail.
verses.before: The seacoast will become pastures, meadows for shepherds and enclosures for flocks.
verses.after: The coast will become pastureland, shepherds’ shelters and pens for flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: The seacoast will become pastures, meadows for shepherds and enclosures for flocks.

verses.rationale: Retains shepherding imagery for the remnant and the restoration idiom.
verses.before: The coastland will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; they will pasture there. In the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down at evening, for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their fortunes.
verses.after: The coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah. There they will graze, and in Ashkelon’s houses they will lie down at evening, for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their fortunes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The coastland will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; they will pasture there. In the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down at evening, for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their fortunes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the territorial aspect and repeated taunting.
verses.before: “I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites, with which they reproached my people and made themselves great against their border.”
verses.after: “I have heard Moab’s taunts and the insults of the Ammonites, who taunted my people and boasted against their territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites, with which they reproached my people and made themselves great against their border.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the oath, both comparisons, and the read my-nation form.
verses.before: So, as I live, declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom, and the Ammonites like Gomorrah: a possession of nettles, a pit of salt, and a desolation forever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and what remains of my nation will possess them.
verses.after: So, as I live,” declares the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, “Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah— a tangle of nettles, a salt pit, a lasting wasteland. The remnant of my people will plunder them; those left of my nation will possess them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, as I live, declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom, and the Ammonites like Gomorrah: a possession of nettles, a pit of salt, and a desolation forever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and what remains of my nation will possess them.

verses.rationale: Connects judgment to the repeated proud taunts without adding motive.
verses.before: This will be theirs in return for their pride, because they reproached and made themselves great against the people of the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: This is what they will receive for their pride, because they taunted and boasted against the people of the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: This will be theirs in return for their pride, because they reproached and made themselves great against the people of the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains the striking starving-gods image and geographically dispersed worship.
verses.before: The LORD will be terrifying against them, for he will make all the gods of the earth waste away; then each person, from their own place, will bow down to him— all the coastlands of the nations.
verses.after: The LORD will be fearsome against them, for he will starve all the gods of the earth. All the coastlands of the nations will bow to him, each from its own place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will be terrifying against them, for he will make all the gods of the earth waste away; then each one, from their own place, will bow down to him— all the coastlands of the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves the abrupt you/they shift instead of treating it as an unnoticed grammatical error.
verses.before: You Cushites also, you will be slain by my sword.
verses.after: “You Cushites too— they will be slain by my sword.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You Cushites also, you will be slain by my sword.

verses.rationale: Keeps both named imperial locations and the dry-wilderness comparison.
verses.before: He will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria; he will make Nineveh a desolation, dry as the wilderness.
verses.after: He will stretch his hand northward and destroy Assyria. He will make Nineveh a wasteland, dry as the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria; he will make Nineveh a desolation, dry as the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Retains architectural ruins and provisional animal identifications with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Flocks will lie down in her midst, every beast of the nation; both desert owl and hedgehog will spend the night among her capitals. A voice will sing in the window; desolation will be on the threshold, for cedarwork has been laid bare.
verses.after: Herds will lie down within her, creatures of every kind. The desert owl and the hedgehog will lodge on her capitals. A voice will sing in the window; ruin will lie on the threshold, for her cedarwork is laid bare.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flocks will lie down in her midst, every beast of the nation; both desert owl and hedgehog will spend the night among her capitals. A voice will sing in the window; desolation will be on the threshold, for cedarwork has been laid bare.

verses.rationale: Keeps the city’s exclusive boast and the scornful gestures.
verses.before: This is the jubilant city, dwelling secure, saying in her heart, “I am, and there is none besides me.” How she has become a desolation, a resting place for wild animals! Everyone who passes by her will hiss and shake a hand.
verses.after: This is the carefree city that lived secure, saying in her heart, “I am, and no one else!” How she has become a wasteland, a resting place for wild animals! Everyone who passes hisses and waves a hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the jubilant city, dwelling secure, saying in her heart, “I am, and there is none besides me.” How she has become a desolation, a resting place for wild animals! Everyone who passes by her will hiss and shake a hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the threefold indictment before the city is named later.
verses.before: Woe to the rebellious and defiled, the oppressing city!
verses.after: Woe to the rebellious, polluted city, the city that oppresses!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the rebellious and defiled, the oppressing city!

verses.rationale: Retains the four negatives and relational progression.
verses.before: She has not listened to the voice; she has not accepted discipline. She has not trusted in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.
verses.after: She has not listened to a voice or accepted correction. She has not trusted the LORD or drawn near to her God.
verses.tsw_comparator: She has not listened to the voice; she has not accepted discipline. She has not trusted in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired predatory offices and the evening/morning contrast.
verses.before: Her officials within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves of the evening— they leave no bones until morning.
verses.after: Her officials within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves at dusk, leaving nothing to gnaw by morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her officials within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves of the evening— they leave no bones until morning.

verses.rationale: Preserves specific male prophets and the violence verb applied to instruction.
verses.before: Her prophets are reckless, treacherous people; her priests have profaned what is holy; they have violated the law.
verses.after: Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men; her priests profane what is holy and do violence to instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her prophets are reckless, treacherous people; her priests have profaned what is holy; they have violated the law.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated morning and the contrast between divine justice and shameless wrongdoers.
verses.before: The LORD is righteous within her; he does no wrong. Morning by morning he brings his justice to light; it does not fail. Yet the unjust know no shame.
verses.after: The LORD within her is righteous; he does no injustice. Morning after morning he brings his judgment to light; he never fails. But the unjust know no shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is righteous within her; he does no wrong. Morning by morning he brings his justice to light; it does not fail. Yet the unjust know no shame.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated absence of inhabitants and the city imagery.
verses.before: “I have cut off nations; their strongholds are desolate. I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through. Their cities are ruined, without people, without an inhabitant.
verses.after: “I have cut off nations; their corner towers are deserted. I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through. Their cities are destroyed, without a person, without an inhabitant.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have cut off nations; their strongholds are desolate. I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through. Their cities are ruined, without people, without an inhabitant.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult you/her/they shifts and the deliberate eagerness to corrupt.
verses.before: I said, ‘Surely you will fear me; you will accept discipline.’ Then her dwelling would not be cut off— all that I had decreed against her. But they rose early to corrupt all their deeds.
verses.after: I said, ‘Surely you will fear me and accept correction.’ Then her dwelling would not be cut off, whatever I had appointed against her. But they rose early to corrupt all their deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, ‘Surely you will fear me; you will accept discipline.’ Then her dwelling would not be cut off— all that I had decreed against her. But they rose early to corrupt all their deeds.

verses.rationale: Follows pointed prey while noting witness alternative and repeats the fire-of-jealousy phrase.
verses.before: So wait for me,” declares the LORD, “for the day when I rise up for plunder. For my judgment is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all the burning of my anger; for all the earth will be consumed by the fire of my jealousy.
verses.after: So wait for me,” declares the LORD, “for the day I rise to seize prey. For my decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour my indignation on them, all my burning anger. The whole earth will be consumed by the fire of my jealousy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore wait for me,” declares the LORD, “for the day when I rise up for plunder. For my judgment is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all the burning of my anger; for all the earth will be consumed by the fire of my jealousy.

verses.rationale: Keeps lips and shared-shoulder images in idiomatic English.
verses.before: “For then I will turn the peoples to a pure speech, that all of them may call on the name of the LORD, to serve him shoulder to shoulder.
verses.after: Then I will give the peoples purified lips, so they may all call on the name of the LORD and serve him shoulder to shoulder.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For then I will turn the peoples to a pure speech, that all of them may call on the name of the LORD, to serve him shoulder to shoulder.

verses.rationale: Treats the difficult daughter-of-my-dispersed phrase collectively with its uncertainty noted.
verses.before: From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers—the daughter of my scattered ones— will bring my offering.
verses.after: From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers, my scattered people, will bring my offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers—the daughter of my scattered ones— will bring my offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves both the removal of proud people and the changed community.
verses.before: On that day you will not be ashamed of all your deeds by which you rebelled against me, for then I will remove from your midst people who exult in your pride, and you will no longer be haughty on my holy mountain.
verses.after: On that day you will no longer be ashamed of all the deeds by which you rebelled against me. For then I will remove from your midst those who revel in your pride; you will no longer be arrogant on my holy mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day you will not be ashamed of all your deeds by which you rebelled against me, for then I will remove from your midst those who exult in your pride, and you will no longer be haughty on my holy mountain.

verses.rationale: Retains material poverty as well as lowliness rather than spiritualizing both terms.
verses.before: Yet I will leave in your midst a people poor and lowly, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
verses.after: I will leave among you a people poor and lowly, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will leave in your midst a people poor and lowly, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves ethical parallels and the peaceful flock image.
verses.before: The remnant of Israel will do no wrong and speak no lie, nor will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouths. For they will pasture and lie down, with no one to make them afraid.
verses.after: The remnant of Israel will do no injustice and speak no lies; no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths. They will graze and lie down, with no one to terrify them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The remnant of Israel will do no wrong and speak no lie, nor will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouths. For they will pasture and lie down, with no one to make them afraid.

verses.rationale: Keeps the feminine city personification and distinct calls to joy.
verses.before: Sing for joy, Daughter Zion! Shout, Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, Daughter Jerusalem!
verses.after: Sing out, daughter Zion! Raise a shout, Israel! Rejoice and celebrate with all your heart, daughter Jerusalem!
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing for joy, Daughter Zion! Shout, Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, Daughter Jerusalem!

verses.rationale: Retains both LORD repetitions and the king designation.
verses.before: The LORD has removed your judgments; he has turned away your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you will fear disaster no more.
verses.after: The LORD has removed the judgments against you and cleared your enemy away. The king of Israel, the LORD, is among you; you will no longer fear harm.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has removed your judgments; he has turned away your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you will fear disaster no more.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily discouragement image in direct encouragement.
verses.before: On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: “Do not fear, Zion; do not let your hands grow slack.
verses.after: On that day Jerusalem will be told: “Do not be afraid, Zion; do not let your hands fall limp.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: “Do not fear, Zion; do not let your hands grow slack.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned be-silent reading instead of silently substituting renew, and retains the warrior image.
verses.before: The LORD your God is in your midst, a mighty warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with gladness; he will be silent in his love; he will exult over you with singing.”
verses.after: The LORD your God is among you, a warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with delight; he will be silent in his love; he will celebrate over you with singing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD your God is in your midst, a mighty warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with gladness; he will be silent in his love; he will exult over you with singing.”

verses.rationale: Marks the return to first-person divine speech, retaining the difficult clause and pronoun change with an explicit note.
verses.before: “I have gathered those grieving over the appointed festival; they were from you. Reproach was a burden upon her.
verses.after: “I will gather those grieving over the appointed festival; they were from you, a burden of reproach upon her.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have gathered those grieving over the appointed festival; they were from you. Reproach was a burden upon her.

verses.rationale: Preserves the vulnerable groups and the reversal of shame, noting the compressed last clause.
verses.before: Look, at that time I will deal with everyone who oppress you. I will save the one who limps and gather the outcast; and I will make them praise and renown in every land where they were put to shame.
verses.after: Look, at that time I will deal with all who oppress you. I will save the lame and gather the outcast. I will give them praise and renown in every land where they were shamed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, at that time I will deal with all who oppress you. I will save the one who limps and gather the outcast; and I will make them praise and renown in every land where they were put to shame.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated time/gathering and the witnessed restoration.
verses.before: At that time I will bring you in, at the time when I gather you. For I will make you renowned and praised among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes,” says the LORD.
verses.after: At that time I will bring you in, at the time I gather you. I will give you renown and praise among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your fortunes before your eyes,” says the LORD.
